The visible steps in a numbered sequence are: 01 — Train Facilitators: Human trains facilitators on CDS design, recruitment, moderation, results analysis, and communication; AI extends human trainer capacities through LLM Assistants and retrieval augmented generation (RAG). 02 — Recruit Participants: Human decides on best approach and selects participants. 03 — Educate Participants: Human curates educational content and diverse perspectives; AI customizes educational materials based on preexisting knowledge, uses generative social choice to convey diversity of expert opinions, and offers a fine-tuned LLM Assistant for interactive Q&A. Arrows indicate the sequence continues to steps 04 and 05, which are partially visible at the ✉️ send the invites
🎵 curate tunes
🍝🍹provide vittles and libations
💡 set an intention for the evening
🚪 make sure no one overstays their welcome

Social media is often full-scale rhetorical warfare. However, that doesn’t mean there shouldn’t be online conflict.

Priya Parker, who has written books on both gathering and fighting, says there is another way: “healthy heat: the willingness to hold tension, with care, long enough for it to become clarifying.”

https://theisolationjournals.substack.com/cp/215506446

"},"interactionPolicy":{"canQuote":{"automaticApproval":["https://www.w3.org/ns/activitystreams#Public"]}},"attachment":[{"type":"Document","mediaType":"image/png","url":"https://files.mastodon.social/media_attachments/files/117/282/677/039/138/118/original/bcb5f65bc82c446e.png","name":"“In twenty-five years as a conflict dialogue facilitator, I’ve learned something deeply counterintuitive: long-term communities need love, and they also need conflict. The relationships that last aren’t the ones that never fight. They’re the ones that learn how to fight well.\n\nAnd yet, when disagreement enters the room, many groups reach for one of two options. We ricochet between unhealthy peace: ghosting, avoiding, quiet resentment, smoothing over with a breezy “No worries!” while privately seething.
